This Appeal Is Coming On For Final Hearing, This Day,
Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
 Judgment

(PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE H.T.NARENDRA PRASAD)
1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act', for short) has been filed by the insurance company challenging the judgment and award dated 01.10.2012 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Gangavathi, in MVC No.120/2012.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that, on 30.03.2011 at about 11:30 pm on Gangavathi Sindhanur main road, near Shripuram junction, while the petitioner's vehicle was returning from Sindhanur to Marali village, at that time, respondent No.1 being the driver of the mini lorry bearing registration No.KA-34/3993 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's vehicle i.e. tata NC: 2024:KHC-D:18003 magic vehicle, on account of which, the petitioner's vehicle was completely damaged.
Hence, the claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
3. Upon service of notice, respondent Nos.1 to 3 appeared through their counsel and filed their objections denying the averments made in the claim petition.
4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has partly allowed the petition awarding compensation of Rs.1,16,248/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realisation.

Being aggrieved, present appeal has been filed by insurance company The Branch Manager, Oriental ... vs Yamanoor S/O Hulugappa on 9 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28215732/

sentences.text: 5. The learned counsel appearing for the insurance company contended that, the claimant's vehicle bearing registration No.KA-37/8612 is insured with NC: 2024:KHC-D:18003 Cholamandalam Insurance Company and a claim petition is filed seeking compensation for the damages to the vehicle.
The claimant has not produced any document to show that he has not made any claim with his insurer and he has not produced the original documents.
Therefore, he is not entitled for compensation.
The Tribunal without considering this aspect of the matter has erred in allowing the claim petition.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal by setting aside the impugned judgment and award.
6. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant has contended that, due to the accident, the claimant's vehicle is completely damaged.
He has produced the quotation as Ex.P4 and P5 wherein it is mentioned that the claimant has spent a sum of Rs.1,20,000/-.
Considering the same, the Tribunal has granted just and reasonable compensation and sought for dismissal of the appeal.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award.

8. It is not in dispute that the claimant's vehicle bearing registration No.KA-37/8612 got damaged in an accident that occurred on 30.03.2011 due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of mini lorry.
The claimant's vehicle is insured with Cholamandalam insurance company.
The claimant has not produced any document to show that he has not made any claim with his insurer.
He has produced the quotations at Exs.P-4 and P-5 for a sum of Rs.1,20,000/-.
He has not produced any receipt for purchasing the spare parts and he has not examined any person from the garage.

Considering the material produced by the claimant, I am of the opinion that the compensation of Rs.1,16,248/- awarded by the Tribunal is on the higher side and the same has to be reduced to Rs.60,000/- globally.

Hence, the following order:
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18003 The appeal is allowed in part.
The judgment and award dated 01.10.2012 passed by the learned Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Gangavathi, in MVC No.120/2012 is modified.
The claimant is entitled to global compensation of Rs.60,000/- without any interest.
The insurance company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount.
Registry is directed to transfer the amount in deposit to the Tribunal concerned.
The Tribunal is directed to refund the excess amount, if any, to the appellant after due verification.

Sd/-
